title: MZ Re Dreams  Demo now available

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
SYNOPSIS
What do you do when life crushes your dreams?  Perhaps you decide to just make the best of a bad job.  Maybe you spend your whole life in bitter resentment.  You might dedicate yourself to getting revenge.  You could simply give up and wither.  But it doesn’t have to be like that.
When you are blackmailed into taking on a job you’d rather not do, and others are press-ganged into joining you, an unexpected consequence is the chance to change, to dream again – but differently.  If, of course, you come out of this alive.
GAMEPLAY
Battle
Order Turn Battle [OTB] System  so you can choose each action as the battle unfolds.   Turn order for current and next turn are visible and there is wide scope to manipulate both your own and the enemy's turn order.
4 difficulty settings.  These can be changed in-game. NOTE at this stage I have not play tested Hard and Veteran.  You are advised to choose Normal or Relaxed.
Once the party is more than 4, you can swap live actors in battle.
At the end of Boss battles you have the choice to continue exactly as you are (including Game Over) or Retry with the HP/MP and items you had at the beginning.  Any cut scene will not be repeated.
The actors do not learn tiered skills.  Skills are powered up by finding Skill Orbs.
Each character has tiered bonuses depending on how many each one personally defeats.
General
6 characters.  The title screen updates each time a character joins, plus at certain late game events.  The title screen shown here reflects the fact that the demo only has 4 characters.
If you hate exploration, this game is probably not for you.  Many items and gear, including some of the best, are found this way.  EXP can also be gained.
Secret Rooms : number still open, but 30+
Side quests (of course) with the choice of  small stat bonuses for each character for every 3 quests completed.
Accomplishments: a Trophy Room awards you a piece of gear on completing certain actions.
Player's Perks awarded at level 10 (so outside the scope of this demo) with improvements at levels 20, 30 and 40.
CURRENT STATE
This is a demo of the first town and dungeon, where you collect your 4th party member.  If you do everything it will take between 1 and 1.5 hours.
Spoiler:
CHARACTERS
I have not yet inserted the short character description of anyone except Robert.  I want to wait until I think that I've nailed their full character concisely.  At the moment they are too long.
Spoiler:
Screenshots
You can download the demo from
here
.
I hope you enjoy it.  Please note the point about which difficulty mode to pick.  Hard and Veteran could well be unplayable yet.
Changelog
9th Dec 2024  passability errors and typos fixed.
12th Dec 2024 Bug fixed and passability errors.
24th Dec 2024 Bug on reentry to Silverley fixed.  QoL additions: Player notified when a quest is added to Quest Journal; all passive skills, not just some, invisible in battle.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
I played this demo, here's some comments [CONTAINS SOME SPOILERS]:
Nice mapping, and character art and I like how music is used in the game. Some of the sideways building entrances where a bit "difficult" to spot though. The story/writing was interesting enough, though for me the character attitudes are a bit too "nonchalant". I mean like the characters (who aren't trained fighters) just casually joking when ambushed etc.  And I'd expect a bigger reaction from Diana in the thief intro, since they did kill her parents. I liked that there were some internal comments by the characters and comments on object interactions.
The battles were ok and the enemies hit hard, but it was too easy to just beat the enemies with standard attacks. Like (at least after gaining a couple of levels) the treants could be killed by just attacking them with all my 3 character's standard attack, before the enemy got a turn. Also, all my characters seemed to have higher agi than any of the enemies.
*Note: The character attacks where showing the rtp weapon animation swing underneath them. Also when jumping back to base an active battler might appear on top of another for a short time.
I like that you find stuff and get simple quests in the houses, that gives exploring some purpose. Like I "hate" games that have big towns with buildings where there's basically nothing inside.
-Sylvia's quest says that I don't have enough money even if I did, unless I go outside first and return
-why did the game ask me if I want to try again when I beat the bandit boss fight?
-after recruiting Diana again and leaving town, the game allows you to continue to an unfinished area where it goes to a black screen if you interact with different stuff

posts.author: Lady_JJ
posts.body:
I did find a few passability and dialogue issues, but I think they've all been identified. I sometimes encounter a lockup with cutscenes. It happened with the party in the passageway after being told to spend the night in the inn, and also in the cutscene with Emma leaving the inn to see Jack and Lily. It's possible that might have been continuing to press the arrow movement key and confusing the cutscene. When I tried to replicate while being careful not to hold any arrow keys down, I couldn't trigger a lockup. However...
I didn't visit Langley Farm before going to the forest. I didn't visit the farm until after Simon was on his way to see the guy about the origin of the medallion and Diane was in the party. When I first spoke to Sam, he warned me about the rabbits and Simon seemed quite surprised, said he'd keep an eye out for them. In reality, he had already seen those rabbits, so he shouldn't have been surprised. Then I went upstairs (and saved, that was a mistake). When I come down the stairs, Sam is there along with 2 other NPCs. Simon reaches the bottom of the stairs, turns to his right, and the game locks up. I repeated it 2 or 3 times with the same results. I restored back to my previous save, before reporting to Wulstan. I can leave town, again with Diane in the party because she doesn't leave until Simon enters the Item Shop, and I get the same lockup result at the farm. If I enter the item shop and let Diane leave the party, and quickly exit the item shop, not going to see Wulstan, I can exit the town, visit the Langley farm, have the same 'Beware of the Rabbits' dialogue with Sam, go upstairs, come down and no lockup. Except, without Diane in the party, when I come downstairs, there's only Sam there. The other two NPC's are not present.
As an aside, I didn't trigger any quest with Sam. I'll go back to the beginning before entering the forest for the first time, visit Langley farm first, and see if any quest gets triggered.
Nice mapping.

It looks as if I'm going to have to do some more work on the dialogue and switches there.  If you only visit the farm for the first time with Diana, you should only have Sam when you come downstairs.  You need to return a bit later (roughly 800 steps, iirc) to find him with his lady friend.

posts.author: Ahuramazda
posts.body:
I really enjoyed the playthrough I did... I played it more of an "actual player" than a 'game tester' when I did it to see if
@Kes
' time estimate was accurate or not, which it was.
To be completely honest I was already getting into the story a bit TOO much - when I got to the message that the demo ended there I was a bit upset that it was already over.
I had played some of the earlier versions of this game and helped debug some of the more major bugs (I ignored most of the main plot dialog in these runs so I wasn't rushing when playing the release version), but nothing like some of the people in this thread are finding.
I too felt the difficulty for battle sometimes was a bit too easy, but sometimes when the RNG wanted to get revenge on you, the fight (esp the Thieves + Leader battle) could really become a nightmare: When every single enemy kept attacking the same party member on the same turn instantly killing them before you could heal/react.
For the beginning of the game though I would say the difficulty is on par enough to keep you mildly engaged, but not so easy you never want to use any items... cant wait to try out the harder game options though.
This is the usual Kes game though, beautiful mapping, well thought out scenes with some witty banter in several locations, kind of light hearted at the start but WILL eventually get into deeper thought and emotional moments later on.
Like their other games, which sadly I have not played them all... but should, honestly... I look forward to see where this little gem goes and what kind of story they come up with in the end.
I know a small amount of the future story and I am eager to see how it gets implemented!
(I know, not much of a useful post, but I wanted to help out with another thread reply since I had no bugs myself besides some of the graphical and pathing ones pointed out already!)

posts.author: Kes
Sword_of_Dusk
posts.body:
Okay, I played this for a just about an hour and a half in order to review it for the Feedback Festival. Couldn't get to the very end of the demo, as the game locks up on me upon trying to reenter Shiverley after recruiting Diana and having the teacher in tow. I've tried multiple times and nothing works. Even so, it was a good run. Let's break it down, shall we?
Spoiler:
The Good
*: What immediately sticks out to me is the dialogue between the party members. You do a lot to give them each their own personality and life. Always good to have characters with some character, especially in an RPG.
*: You do a good job of impressing upon the player what kind of world they are entering, but without it being particularly egregious with how you do it. Life in the city feels unfair as hell, and that's a good thing if you want people to empathize with the protags.
*: Each character having unique passive skills helps give them individuality beyond their active skill sets. Also serves as another way to inform the player of their personalities.
*: Entering NPC homes isn't just some thing you do in order to rob them blind. There's conversations to be had, and some people really don't want to be disturbed. Makes the place feel like a true city.
*: You're rewarded for exploration. That's a key thing I'm always looking for in a game, and you do good here.
*: Combat isn't a chore. It's a fairly simple affair and I don't feel like I'm banging my head against a wall in order to clear a fight.
*: The party has solid artwork and I don't hate looking at it.
*: Options aplenty! Thank you for giving the player several options to tweak their experience.
Spoiler:
The Bad
*: Combat isn't a chore, but it does feel somewhat unbalanced. Enemies die in roughly two hits, but they also hit just as hard. That's fine when you're up against one or two foes, but if there's a situation where you get outnumbered, I can forsee it being a rough experience. The boss fight against the thieves is a perfect example. They hit harder than standard foes, and all it takes is some unlucky RNG for them to drop someone almost instantly. If someone does die, you're basically done at that point.
*: Related to combat, it's really basic at the start. Doubly so for Robert, who can't really do crap until stealing a skill. I can see that being problematic as the game goes on, as you'll either have him picking up skills too quickly or find his combat poor because he's got little to call upon until he does manage to steal a few skills.
*: While the party's artwork is good, Conrad and Wulstan look really odd to me. Conrad especially looks like the product of AI, but I see you've already confirmed that's not the case. Even still, neither man really fits in with the way the party looks. Consistency between portraits would be stellar.
*: It's really odd that Robert comes pre-equipped with his staff, but you have to equip Simon and Emma. I'd rather have them all equipped to begin with. You can't access the menu before they receive their equipment, so the player wouldn't know anything.
*: Small thing, but it's annoying seeing the passive skills in the battle menu. I don't really like needing to navigate through them when picking another skill. They should really only be viewable in the field.
*: There's no alert for when you pick up a quest. It's not a major issue since you can mostly tell when something is worth remembering, but I can see some players not realizing anything until they happen to check the quest log.
*: The aforementioned locking up of the game. I cannot reach the very end of the demo because I can't get back into town. Perhaps doing so without Diana would allow me to progress, but I haven't gotten around to replaying it in order to figure that out yet. Probably want to look into this.
This is the first review I've done for anything in a long, long time, so sorry if it isn't quite as eloquent as others might be. I am looking forward to spending more time with the game though. I will be keeping an eye on it.

posts.author: TRIDIUM
posts.body:
Review time!
Spoiler
-I'm sure this was placeholder, but the first splash screen needs to be fixed
-The options menu was  bit difficult to navigate.
-I have a bit of a rant about the game's sound.
For the most part, it's good. I like a lot of the music, it's nice and quiet and fits the maps. The audio design for background noise is also really good. I like that the water sounds louder the closer you are to it. That's all great.
There's a lack of sound sometimes that can be weird. For example, when introducing the new characters, it feels like there should be a little flourish or something, considering the art. There were a few cutscenes that could have used some different music as well.
I also found the UI sound effects to be frustratingly off. Like they felt every so slightly too late after you selected something.
The RTP sound effects in battle were a bit disappointing as well, specifically the monster death noise.
-I thought the maps were really well done, and looked great
-UI was fine. Sometimes it felt a little overwhelming, but otherwise fine.
-The character art for the faces was really good. If you did get full body art for characters, I would suggest not just using the face box, and use busts. That's a personal pet peeve, but I do think busts look better unless it's pixel art.
-Personally, I find Simon's green jumpsuit to be a bit loud and out of place in the medieval setting.
-I'm not a fan of the tall sprites with RTP heads. I don't think it really fits the mood and other art in the game. Also, Simon and Emma's sprites were really hard to tell apart.
-The rabbits in the forest seem to change color randomly
-The paragraph formatting in message boxes doesn't always look right. I think it's a VS issue, I've had the same issue in my game.
-I know it's a little thing, but I really like how the doors work in your game. They felt way more natural.
-You can walk over the trees in the main town.
-The world map was a bit confusing. There were a few invisible walls and it took a while to find the forest.
-The combat was fine. I'm not sure what the purpose of the lower AGI skill was, as they went last anyway or would die that turn. Also, it's a small thing, but it's kind of weird that the huge tree monster was weaker than like two rabbits.
-Exploration was great, and the balance of items and such felt good.
-I'm not sure what the purpose of the save demon NPC was. You could save anyway, and she doesn't heal you, so...
-I stopped playing after dying in the bar fight with the thieves. I reloaded my save, and went back to the main town to complete the scholar quest. When I entered the town, it played the quest end cutscene twice and than froze.
-The story was okay. It felt like it moved a bit too fast, and I didn't get a real sense of the world I was in.
-I did like your main party though. Simon was bit generic, but the other two were great. I'm glad you didn't go with the usual band of tropey teens.
-The little bits of dialogue was cool, and I like the idea, but maybe make it a popup window, as not to get in the way of combat?
-It's a bit weird that you can barge into random people's houses, and sometimes they sort of react to it, but not in a way that feels natural. I would stick with either not addressing it entirely, or make it more realistic.

posts.author: punitdh89
posts.body:
Just finished playing your game, and I've gotta say of all the RPG Maker games I've played recently, this was definitely one of the better ones.
I really appreciated the effort you put into systems. The quest log was a great inclusion (Though I'll admit, I wish there was a mini-map or compass. There was one point I spent over 20 minutes trying to find Wulstan again after forgetting where he was).
The dialog system was solid. There weren't any choices, but the writing itself was actually quite decent, and a far cry from the low-effort jokes or filler I've seen otherwise.
The UI was also excellent
.
I don't say that lightly. Clean, readable and fit the atmosphere perfectly. Loved it.
The battle system was fun, too. I liked that agility actually mattered in turn order. I'm still using default turn-based in my own project, so it was refreshing to see something more dynamic.
Just as a side note: I found the bandit battles a bit too difficult. I think they do too much damage each. I had to go back to the forest and grind for XP before returning to battle the bandits. Even at the lowest difficulty, took me about 15+ tries to beat them.
The loot system was also great. I liked how items were visually placed in the world instead of just coming from chests or monster drops. Though admittedly, the loot felt mostly like junk? Useful for selling, but with no crafting or secondary purpose (yet?).
The stat upgrade system (collecting orbs) was awesome and I hope you do more of it The small pop-up messages whenever I picked up loot were a nice bit of polish.
But the best thing I liked was that the fact that your characters actually comment on the battles
.
Fighting treants or rabbits, they always had something to say. That really kept me engaged.
Maybe for the future, you can also add some random dialog lines, so that the players don't always say the same thing for each battle. Just a suggestion.
Keep it up, and looking forward to the next release.
